candidates.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv with Economy Minister Katherina Reiche and German defense-industry executives. German officials said he would announce €1 billion in military aid and €350 million for energy-system repairs; the visit was also expected to advance, but had not yet finalized, agreements on joint drone and long-range weapons production.
candidates.title: German Chancellor Merz arrives in Kyiv with aid and defense-industry delegation

candidates.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung ordered a thorough investigation and response measures after hacking incidents caused personal-data leaks at banks, other financial companies and public institutions. The presidential office said authorities were instructed to treat the matter seriously and develop countermeasures.
candidates.title: South Korean president orders investigation into financial-sector data breaches

candidates.summary: North Korean state media said leader Kim Jong Un supervised a test of an intermediate-range hypersonic missile. KCNA said the missile was launched from eastern North Korea on October 3 and struck a target about 1,000 kilometers away in waters off the east coast. The claimed test details were not independently verified in the initial report.
candidates.title: North Korea announces hypersonic missile test supervised by Kim Jong Un

candidates.summary: With 97% of ballots counted after Latvia's October 3 parliamentary election, Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' centrist United List led with 35.3%, corresponding to a projected 42 seats in the 100-seat parliament. The result was provisional, with coalition negotiations still required and final official results pending certification.
candidates.title: Latvia's United List leads provisional parliamentary election results

sources.name: Latvia Central Election Commission turnout data

candidates.summary: Brazilians began first-round voting in a general election led by the presidential contest between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Nearly 159 million people were eligible to vote; the election also covers Congress, governorships and state legislatures. No outcome had been established during the coverage interval.
candidates.title: Brazil begins voting in presidential and general elections

candidates.summary: Yemen's Saudi-backed Presidential Leadership Council chief Rashad al-Alimi announced the start of military operations intended to retake Houthi-held territory and extend government authority nationwide. Government-aligned forces said they were conducting strikes against Houthi targets in Sanaa and Saada; Houthi-run media attributed an attack on Sanaa to Saudi Arabia, which had not immediately confirmed that claim.
candidates.title: Yemen's government announces operation to retake Houthi-held territory

candidates.summary: Thousands of young demonstrators and opposition supporters rallied in New Delhi and Mumbai for a third consecutive day, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and reversal of electoral-roll revisions. Police detained demonstrators. Kumar had not responded publicly, while the Election Commission said the revisions were intended to remove duplicate, deceased or ineligible entries.
candidates.title: Indian protests demanding election commissioner's resignation escalate

candidates.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard said Chinese vessels obstructed a Philippine operation against a foreign fishing vessel suspected of blast fishing near Philippine-held Thitu Island. It described the presence of a Chinese navy helicopter as intimidation. The Chinese Embassy in Manila had not immediately commented on the Philippine account.
candidates.title: Philippines says Chinese vessels obstructed operation near Thitu Island

candidates.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said Russian forces struck Kyiv's Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River on Sunday, describing it as a route for military personnel and cargo. The claim was not independently verified in the initial report and Ukrainian authorities had not been cited as confirming the target or damage.
candidates.title: Russia claims strike on Kyiv bridge over Dnipro River

candidates.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton would additionally serve as White House artificial-intelligence czar and lead a new Super Intelligence Force. Trump said the body would coordinate federal engagement with public-interest groups, infrastructure providers and AI companies.
candidates.title: Trump names intelligence director Jay Clayton as White House AI czar

candidates.summary: The British government announced it would abandon plans to remove jury trials for defendants in less serious criminal cases after sustained criticism from lawyers and politicians. The announcement withdrew the proposal rather than changing trial rights immediately through enacted legislation.
candidates.title: British government drops proposal to restrict jury trials

candidates.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced €1 billion in additional military aid and €350 million for energy-system repairs during his Kyiv visit. German executives signed 14 agreements with Ukrainian government and business counterparts worth about €6.6 billion, including agreements involving IRIS-T missiles, radar equipment and jet-drone interceptors. Ukraine and Germany said a broader defense-production agreement remained under negotiation.
candidates.title: Merz announces German aid and defense agreements during Kyiv visit

candidates.summary: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said a Russian strike hit the Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River, damaging its roadway and a nearby hot-water system and injuring two people. Russia's Defence Ministry described the bridge as a route used to transport military personnel and cargo.
candidates.title: Kyiv confirms damage and injuries from Russian strike on Northern Bridge

candidates.summary: Polls closed in Brazil's first-round general election after voting led by the presidential contest between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The electoral court chief said the election had proceeded normally as of Sunday afternoon. Results remained pending; a presidential runoff would be held October 25 if no candidate received more than half of valid votes.
candidates.title: Polls close in Brazil's presidential and general elections

candidates.summary: Iranian state media said President Masoud Pezeshkian accepted Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad's resignation and appointed National Iranian Oil Company chief Hamid Bovard as acting minister. No reason for the resignation was initially provided.
candidates.title: Iranian oil minister resigns and state oil-company chief becomes acting minister

candidates.summary: Britain's Green Party conference approved a motion describing Zionism as a form of racism by 1,022 votes to 813. The party said the motion also backed Palestinian and Jewish rights and called for one democratic state across historic Palestine. British Jewish groups and Israel's government condemned the decision; Israel said party leader Zack Polanski would be barred from entering the country.
candidates.title: British Green Party adopts motion defining Zionism as racism

candidates.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina completed voting for its tripartite presidency, national parliament and regional legislatures. Preliminary results from about 80% of polling stations showed Denis Bećirović and Željka Cvijanović leading the Bosniak and Serb presidential races, respectively, while Darijana Filipović led the Croat contest. The results remained provisional.
candidates.title: Preliminary results reported in Bosnia and Herzegovina's general election

sources.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina Central Election Commission

candidates.summary: Austrian Vice Chancellor Andreas Babler said he would leave that post and the leadership of the governing Social Democratic Party in early 2027 amid internal concern about declining poll support. Babler said Finance Minister Markus Marterbauer would succeed him as vice chancellor, though the precise timing had not been set.
candidates.title: Austrian Vice Chancellor Andreas Babler announces planned departure

candidates.summary: The Pentagon confirmed that all U.S. B-1 bombers deployed to RAF Fairford had returned to their home stations in the United States. It did not disclose when the aircraft moved. The confirmation followed arrests connected to an alleged plot against the British base; Iran denied British claims linking it to the suspected plot.
candidates.title: Pentagon confirms B-1 bombers redeployed from British base

candidates.summary: The Australian Federal Police said a joint counterterrorism team was investigating the Flydubai FZ1073 co-pilot's connections to Australia. Sources told Reuters that the co-pilot, accused of stabbing the captain and attempting to hijack the aircraft, had studied in Melbourne. The investigation had not established Australian involvement in the attack.
candidates.title: Australian counterterrorism team investigates Flydubai co-pilot's local links
